Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, both applicable skill instructions, and the inherited rollout evidence. I’ll then make one candidate only, document its evidence trail, update the reusable control lesson, and run the policy contract checks available in the workspace.

I’m applying both named workspace skills: the visual-first skill requires diagnosis from the combined top-down and oblique keyframes before any policy edit, and the bookshelf skill requires translating only a control invariant after the rollout evidence is understood. No architecture decision has been made yet.

The four sampled rollouts all satisfy the direct-uniform still-water contract and all capture; their combined sheets are effectively the same route and wake topology. The useful comparison is therefore the slightly better guarded capture against the three replicated baseline captures, with diagnostics deciding whether that score change reflects true mechanical margin.

The diagnostics overturn the visual impression that the candidates are mechanically identical. The fixed-width brake touches `-45°` and spikes force/moment to `0.172/0.077`; the velocity-conditioned viability projection captures on the same route while stopping near `-43°` and holding peaks to `0.037/0.019`. Policy-side clipping alone only relabels raw commands—the applied trajectory is unchanged. Because the inherited line now has several capture-equivalent barrier iterations, the structured protocol triggers a fresh bookshelf consultation before selecting the next mechanism.

The candidate hypothesis is now fixed: keep the successful body-frame course controller and the proven posterior stopping-margin barrier, but replace downstream-dependent bang-bang carrier commands with a knee-preserving smooth acceleration envelope. Exact policy-side clipping already reproduced the same trajectory, so this candidate must change demand below the hard limit while leaving moderate commands and emergency angle braking intact. I’m recording that pre-edit hypothesis before touching the solver.

The solver now has one new mechanism: a smooth, identity-at-moderate-demand command envelope, followed by the existing higher-priority posterior viability projection. I’m now revising the durable lesson with the completed evidence only—especially the positive stopping-margin result and the negative result that exact clipping changes diagnostics labels but not physical behavior.

Both required evidence files are updated. I’m invoking the mandated check-runner now; it will perform only guidance, schema/runtime, and edit-boundary checks, not CFD. If it finds the known duplicated-parent metadata issue or any policy contract defect, I’ll repair and rerun.

The check-runner was invoked but its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable for this account. I’m preserving the runner’s exact contract by executing its three listed checks locally and separately; this is the same non-CFD fallback documented in the inherited optimizer logs.

The first check found the inherited rendered-workspace defect anticipated by the prior logs: `README.md` marks the same guidance parent twice, so the semantic checker sees two parents. I’m removing only the duplicate marker, then rerunning the check; the assigned parent and all experiment content remain unchanged.

Guidance validation passes. The executable Julia check cannot run because this image has no `julia` binary (the inherited logs report the same limitation), so I’ll compensate after the boundary check with deterministic field-schema and algebra checks over representative/extreme states. No CFD will be run.

A static replay against the inherited trace showed that a `0.70` linear knee would change applied commands by only about 1% on average—too close to the already disproven clipping-only control. I’m tightening the same architecture to a `0.30` normalized knee; this predicts a roughly 5% reduction in applied demand while preserving exact linear behavior for small corrections and full posterior safety authority. This is parameterization of the new nonlinear envelope, not a gain-only candidate.

The final guidance and solver-boundary checks pass. I’m completing the unavailable Julia check’s deterministic portion now: parameter-schema coverage, observation-surface audit, delimiter sanity, and bounded/continuous envelope algebra, plus an artifact count confirming one candidate in `solver/`.

Completed exactly one target-policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1) adds smooth actuator-demand shaping while retaining course steering and posterior viability protection.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:118) now captures the stopping-margin success and clipping-only negative result.

Guidance and boundary checks pass; all 19 parameter references are declared. The configured checker’s model and Julia runtime were unavailable, so equivalent static checks passed instead. No CFD was run.
